article.title: MAGA-Coded ‘60 Minutes’ Humiliated by Ratings Crash
article.summary: Mark Seliger/60 Minutes/CBSThe revamped 60 Minutes premiered to its smallest audience in a quarter-century.The once-storied news program opened Sunday night to an audience of about 7.7 million, according to preliminary Nielsen ratings, marking the lowest viewership for the newsmagazine’s season opener since at least the turn of the century.The CBS staple returns for its 59th season under the leadership of CBS News Editor-in-ChiefBari Weiss, a former conservative blogger with no previous experience running a television newsroom, and tech columnist-turned-executive producerNick Bilton.Read more at The Daily Beast.

article.title: Bari Weiss smacked with 'pretty striking drop' as early returns come in for '60 Minutes'
article.summary: "60 Minutes" is off to a rough start in its first full season under CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.The long-running CBS newsmagazine drew about 7.7 million viewers for its season opener, its smallest premiere audience in records dating back to at least 2000, and, year over year, the premiere was down 19 percent among total viewers and 33 percent in the key 25-to-54 demographic, the early figures showed,reported the New York Post."Final Nielsen numbers for Sunday will be available this afternoon,"CNN's Brian Stelter posted on BlueSky. "But preliminary numbers landed this morning, and a top TV exec tells me it 'looks like the '60 Minutes' premiere will be down more than 20%' versus the season premiere last year. The number to beat from last September was 10 million.""To be fair, the exec said, 'the NFL lead-in is weaker this year,'" Stelter added. "'And there have been Nielsen methodology changes. article.title: Begun, the Bari Weiss Era at 60 Minutes Has... But for How Long?
MAGA-Curious CBS Boss’ Secret Calls to Hegseth’s Wife Revealed
article.summary: Leigh Vogel/Getty Images for Uber, X and The Free Press-Evelyn Hockstein/ReutersCBS News boss Bari Weiss leaned on Pete Hegseth’s wife to secure an interview with an American airman rescued in Iran, it has emerged.The airman, identified only as Bravo, spoke to Norah O’Donnell for Sunday’s season premiere of60 Minutes, which Weiss has sought to revamp during her tenure at the nowTrump-friendly network.Bravo was one oftwo airmenrescued in April after their F-15E fighter jet was shot down over Iran. During the interview, Bravo described how he avoided enemy capture for 48 hours and scaled a mountain to be rescued while suffering from a broken back. He said he survived by living by the “warrior ethos” Hegseth demands of all service members.Read more at The Daily Beast.

article.title: '60 Minutes' exposé shocks as viewers ask how it 'made it past' MAGA-coded Bari Weiss
article.summary: CBS News’ “60 Minutes” aired an explosive exposé Sunday night revealing new details about the emerging pardon industry under the second Trump administration, and several critics were shocked that the segment managed to air under the leadership of CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss.Using a fake pardon-seeker with hidden cameras, CBS News’ investigation found that Trump-connected brokers were charging clemency applicants fees reaching as high as $3 million to lobby for presidential pardons outside the traditional Justice Department (DOJ) review process, with “about 70%” of President Donald Trump's second-term clemency actions bypassing DOJ vetting entirely.“If this is the version that made it past Bari Weiss, how bad is the real story?” askedJoe Flood, a D.C.-based writer and photographer, in asocial media poston X.Weiss, who’scozied up to billionairesin her ascent to CBS’ top leadership role, has faced scrutiny for her leadership at CBS News, including for thecontroversial firingof ...
